news.summary: As concern grows regarding the dangers of artificial intelligence, AI regulation has become a hot topic in both Silicon Valley and Washington, D.C.AI giant Anthropic, the maker of Claude, has been pitching its own set of AI safety rules to lawmakers, and Politico recently obtained a confidential draft of the company's proposals.So, what's in Anthropic's proposed AI safety bill? Let's just say at least some of these proposals is eye-opening, to say the least.According to the document obtained by Politico, Anthropic's AI safety bill would only allow the government to block the release of an AI model if it posed a "foreseeable, imminent risk" of causing more than $1 billion in damages or the death or serious injury of more than 50 people.Want more tech and digital culture news delivered to your inbox daily or sent straight to your device? According to the proposal seen by Politico, independent evaluators would periodically analyze an AI lab and its models. If the evaluators find that there is an "imminent enumerated risk" from a model, they would report it to the U.S. Commerce Department within 72 hours. The Commerce Department would then decide if the threshold for a risk requires a request for a judge to block the release of the model. PHP vulnerability: PHP security issues today explained
news.summary: The team behind PHP released emergency security updates on Wednesday to fix two critical vulnerabilities, a day after details about the flaws leaked online. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to install the fix immediately.What is PHP?PHP is a programming language that runs on web servers. When you load a webpage, PHP often runs behind the scenes, retrieving data from databases and building the page before it reaches your browser. BleepingComputer notes that it powers many websites, including content management systems, online stores, and custom web services. According to the NCSC, PHP is also built into a range of other products.The NCSC says the two flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, could allow an attacker to run their own commands on a PHP-based server without logging in. This is called remote code execution, and it's one of the most serious kinds of security bugs.According to the NCSC, an attacker could overload PHP's memory to corrupt it, then, under certain conditions, use that corruption to take control of the server.

news.title: ‘This Is Not a Drill’: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Are Setting the Internet on Fire
news.summary: Internet security and web administration teams around the world are scrambling to prevent widespread disaster. On Wednesday, the developers behind the much-used PHP programming language released emergency security updates designed to fix critical flaws that could be exploited to allow attackers to gain dangerous remote control of victim systems. The PHP Foundation detailed the two critical vulnerabilities—CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619—which impact “all PHP installations serving web requests” going back to PHP version 5, released in July 2004. However, only PHP 8.2 and newer are still supported and will receive patches, according to the alert. The PHP Foundation noted, though, that some PHP distributions and third-party vendors still produce legacy fixes. The caveat is significant, because ubiquitous and foundational web layers like PHP can persist forgotten and un-updated in historic internet infrastructure.

news.title: AI Guardrails Aren’t Stopping Criminal Hackers
news.summary: As AI adoption spreads among both malicious hackers and defenders, even relatively unsophisticated cybercriminals are incorporating agentic AI into their campaigns and getting around model safeguards, according to new details published on Wednesday about recent successful attacks by four different threat groups. Researchers from the threat intelligence firm CrowdStrike looked at the AI infrastructure powering attacks perpetrated between May and August by four previously unreported groups—one that operates in Chinese, one in Spanish and English, one in Indonesian, and one in Russian. The former two exhibited sophisticated AI “harnesses,” the software that supports and guides a model to carry out tasks. The latter two showed less technical prowess, researchers found, but were still able to compromise multiple targets. All had left their AI infrastructure openly accessible on web servers, allowing the researchers to analyze their activity and which models they used—largely versions of Anthropic’s Claude as well as versions of the open-weight Deepseek models. All the actors devised ways to allow their campaigns to run autonomously over relatively long periods of time.

news.title: The new economics of enterprise AI

Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal. Alliance Arts isn’t alone in taking a more defensive stance toward sharing ideas. Papers, Please developer Lucas Pope said on an April podcast that, in general, “you don’t really talk about stuff when you’re working on it because I don’t know it’s going to get slurped up by AI or people are going to copy it or something else like that… I just didn’t feel as comfortable talking about the stuff I was working on again.”

news.title: Public benefit fund
news.summary: Today, Anthropic is committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline. As a public benefit corporation, most of Anthropic's work in pursuit of Anthropic's mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so Anthropic house them directly in the company. The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling Anthropic to pursue Anthropic's mission in new ways: for example, Anthropic might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.
